questions.q: In “sales rose from €40,000 to €55,000”, what does “from €40,000” identify?
options: The starting sales level
The final sales level
The amount of the increase
The rate of the increase
questions.explanation: From introduit le niveau de départ ; to introduit le niveau d’arrivée. Le montant et le taux de variation constituent encore deux informations différentes.

questions.q: A chart shows 80 employees in January and 95 in June. Which sentence preserves the direction and period of the change?
options: Headcount reached 80 in June, up from 95 in January.
Headcount rose from 80 in January to 95 in June.
Headcount rose from 95 in January to 80 in June.
Headcount fell from 80 in January to 95 in June.
questions.explanation: La description doit conserver les deux niveaux, leurs dates et le sens de la variation. Inverser les dates ou employer fell déforme la trajectoire montrée.

questions.q: A chart uses thousands of euros, but a summary copies its labels and describes them simply as euros. What is the main reporting error?
options: An observed result has become a forecast.
A relative change has become a percentage-point change.
The measurement scale has been lost.
The starting and ending dates have been reversed.
questions.explanation: Une échelle en milliers doit rester visible dans le commentaire. Copier les seuls nombres en euros change les montants, même si le sens de la variation est conservé.

questions.q: One chart reports monthly sales in euros and another reports annual sales in euros. Which comparability problem is explicitly shown?
options: The figures use different currencies.
One figure is a volume and the other a monetary value.
One figure is a profit and the other a sales amount.
The reporting periods differ.
questions.explanation: Comparer un mois et une année sans retraitement mélange deux périmètres temporels. Les deux séries portent pourtant sur des ventes en euros : ces caractéristiques sont communes.

questions.q: The source says “revenue fell to €90,000”. A summary says “revenue fell by €90,000”. What has changed?
options: An ending level has been replaced by a change amount.
A change amount has been replaced by a starting level.
A sales amount has been replaced by an expense amount.
A current observation has been replaced by a future promise.
questions.explanation: To indique le niveau atteint, tandis que by indique l’ampleur de la baisse. Les deux phrases n’énoncent pas la même information financière.

questions.q: A table contains two divisions, but the accompanying sentence reports “total company sales”. What must be established before using that wording?
options: That both divisions use the same reporting currency, even if other divisions are omitted.
That the table covers the company’s full sales perimeter
That sales rose in both divisions, regardless of sales outside the table.
That the two divisions have equal sales, even if the company contains additional activities.
questions.explanation: Une somme portant sur deux divisions ne représente le total de l’entreprise que si le périmètre est complet. Le commentaire ne doit pas élargir silencieusement le champ des données.

questions.q: Which sentence reports the magnitude of a relative increase rather than a final amount?
options: Revenue stood at €12 million.
Revenue was €12 million at year-end.
Revenue increased by 12%.
Revenue increased to €12 million.
questions.explanation: By 12% exprime un taux de variation. Les trois autres phrases donnent un niveau de chiffre d’affaires, sans chiffrer l’ampleur de la hausse.

questions.q: A report separately states that sales rose by €5,000 and gives a relative growth rate. Which additional figure is needed to verify that rate?
options: The final sales figure used as the denominator without subtracting the increase.
The increase itself, used as both the numerator and the comparison base.
The average of opening and closing sales, used instead of the stated initial base.
The initial sales amount used as the comparison base
questions.explanation: Une variation relative rapporte l’écart à une base initiale. Des montants concernant les produits, la banque ou le capital ne fournissent pas cette base de ventes.

questions.q: Two divisions report the same absolute sales increase but different initial sales levels. A writer assigns them the same growth rate. What is the problem?
options: Equal absolute changes can represent different relative changes.
Equal absolute changes must have opposite signs.
Growth rates do not depend on the comparison base.
Each division’s final level must equal the absolute change.
questions.explanation: Le taux dépend de l’écart et du niveau de départ. Un même supplément de ventes pèse davantage sur une petite base que sur une grande base.

questions.q: A source states “sales increased by 8% compared with last year”. Which information must remain in a faithful summary?
options: The same 8% figure presented as a comparison with the previous month.
The 8% change and its year-on-year comparison base
The 8% figure presented as the company’s current market share.
The year-on-year comparison presented as an 8% increase in the level of profit.
questions.explanation: Le chiffre de 8% n’a de sens qu’avec sa référence temporelle. La phrase ne donne pas automatiquement un montant absolu ni une prévision pour l’année suivante.

questions.q: A chart begins at zero sales. A student divides the increase by that starting value to report a conventional growth percentage. What should the commentary state?
options: The rate is 100% whenever sales move from zero to a positive amount.
The rate is zero because the starting value is zero.
A conventional relative growth rate cannot be calculated using a zero base.
The final positive amount can serve directly as the conventional percentage increase.
questions.explanation: Une division par une base nulle ne fournit pas un taux de variation classique exploitable. Il faut décrire l’évolution autrement, par exemple en montant et en niveau atteint.

questions.q: Which expression normally describes the difference between two percentage rates?
options: A change in currency units
A change in headcount units
A change in calendar months
A change in percentage points
questions.explanation: Une différence entre deux taux s’exprime en points de pourcentage. Cette unité se distingue des euros, des effectifs ou de la durée observée.

questions.q: A table says that delivery times "ranged from 4 to 9 days". Which description preserves the meaning of this range?
options: The reported minimum was 4 days and the maximum was 9 days.
The average delivery took 4 days and every delivery took no more than 4 days.
Every delivery took exactly the midpoint between 4 and 9 days.
The delivery time increased from 4 days to 9 days during the period.
questions.explanation: Ranged from…to describes the bounds of the reported values. It does not by itself describe a mean, a common value or a change over time.

questions.q: An English report says that "one in four respondents" selected an option. What proportion does this expression describe?
options: Four respondents out of each hundred.
A quarter of the respondents.
Four respondents for each one who selected another option.
One respondent fewer than the four previously reported.
questions.explanation: One in four means one out of every four, or a quarter. It expresses a proportion rather than a four-percent rate, a four-to-one ratio or a subtraction.

questions.q: A chart presents both “relative growth” and “percentage-point change” for a market share. What should an English commentary do?
options: Use percent and percentage points interchangeably when both refer to the same market share.
Keep only the numerical values and leave the reader to infer which measure each uses.
Name the measure used each time it cites a change.
Present the relative change as the final share and the point change as its initial level.
questions.explanation: Les deux mesures peuvent décrire la même évolution sous des angles différents. Le lecteur doit savoir si le commentaire parle d’un écart de taux ou d’une variation rapportée à une base.

questions.q: An analyst subtracts two profit margins, then labels the result “growth relative to the initial margin” without dividing by the initial margin. Which correction is appropriate?
options: Keep the relative-growth label because subtracting two percentage rates automatically produces a relative rate.
Call the difference the final profit margin, without adding it to the initial margin.
Divide the difference by the final margin but continue to label it as growth relative to the initial margin.
Label the subtraction as a percentage-point change.
questions.explanation: La soustraction de deux marges donne leur écart en points. Une croissance relative demanderait de rapporter cet écart à la marge initiale.

questions.q: An English summary says “the interest rate rose by one point” for an international audience. Which revision makes the unit explicit?
options: The interest rate rose by one percentage point.
The interest rate rose by one percent relative to its previous level.
The interest rate rose to one percent.
The interest rate rose by one hundred percent of its previous level.
questions.explanation: Percentage point précise l’unité de l’écart de taux et évite l’ambiguïté de point. Il ne faut pas introduire une référence au chiffre d’affaires absente de la source.

questions.q: Which statement distinguishes an observed association from a proven cause?
options: The two measures moved together, which is sufficient to identify the direction of causation.
The two measures moved together, but this does not establish causation.
The association establishes causation once the variables are expressed in the same unit.
The association becomes causal when it appears in more than one graph from the same dataset.
questions.explanation: Une association temporelle ou statistique ne suffit pas à prouver une cause. D’autres facteurs ou un mécanisme inverse peuvent expliquer les mouvements observés.

questions.q: Sales rose after an advertising campaign, but the same period included a general market recovery. Which sentence is best supported?
options: The rise after the campaign estimates its separate effect, even though the market recovered at the same time.
The common timing of the campaign and recovery allows their individual contributions to be identified directly.
Sales rose after the campaign; the market recovery may also have contributed.
The campaign’s effect equals the whole sales increase after subtracting no contribution for the recovery.
questions.explanation: Les données autorisent un constat et plusieurs explications possibles. Elles ne permettent pas d’isoler la contribution de la campagne sans analyse supplémentaire.

questions.q: Read: "The survey compared delivery speed and reliability. The latter received the higher rating." Which aspect received the higher rating?
options: Delivery speed.
Both aspects received an equal rating.
The aspect measured in the earlier survey, regardless of the order named here.
Reliability.
questions.explanation: The latter refers to the second of the two items just mentioned, reliability. The former would refer to delivery speed.

questions.q: A small observational dataset links training attendance with higher productivity. What would strengthen a causal claim?
options: Examining alternative factors and the way participants were selected
Treating the observed difference as the effect of training without examining differences between attendees and non-attendees.
Increasing the number of observations from the same selected group while assuming selection can no longer matter.
Replacing the initial comparison with the final productivity level alone, without considering the starting situations.
questions.explanation: Une analyse causale doit examiner les explications concurrentes et la sélection des personnes formées. Une formulation plus affirmative ne remplace pas ces contrôles.

questions.q: A dashboard contains no cost data. The writer concludes that higher revenue proves higher profit. Which limitation should be stated?
options: A sales dashboard necessarily measures every component of net profit.
Profit cannot be inferred from revenue growth alone without relevant cost information.
Revenue growth means profit must change by the same amount.
The absence of cost data proves costs were unchanged.
questions.explanation: Le bénéfice dépend aussi des charges du périmètre étudié. L’absence d’information sur les coûts ne permet ni de les supposer constants ni de garantir une amélioration du résultat.
